# op — OpenProject CLI

Lightweight Perl CLI for the [OpenProject](https://www.openproject.org/) REST API (v3). Zero non-core Perl dependencies.

## Example Usage

```bash
tools/op help                      # show help
tools/op project list              # list all projects
tools/op project create "Neo-Mach" neo-mach
tools/op project get <id|slug>
tools/op project update 3 name="New Name"
tools/op project delete <id|slug>

tools/op wp list                   # list tickets in default project
tools/op wp list --status New --priority High
tools/op wp list --project gnu-mach-hurd
tools/op wp create "Port USB stack" --type Milestone --priority High
tools/op wp update 42 status="In progress" subject="Updated"
tools/op wp delete 42
tools/op wp types|statuses|priorities   # reference data

tools/op config                    # show active .env settings
```

## Configuration

Read from `.env` in the project root:

| Variable | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `OPENPROJECT_URL` | Server base URL (e.g. `http://localhost:8080`) |
| `OPENPROJECT_ACCESS_TOKEN` | Bearer token |
| `OPENPROJECT_USERNAME` | Display user |
| `OPENPROJECT_PROJECT_ID` | Default target project for `wp` commands |

Override the default project with `--project <id|slug>` on any `wp` subcommand.

## Dependencies

Only core Perl modules (v5.28+): `LWP::UserAgent`, `HTTP::Request`, `JSON::PP`, `Getopt::Long`. No CPAN installs needed.

# 00 — North Star

## The vision (one paragraph)

Build **Kainos-Logos**: a machine where a *neural language kernel* translates messy
human input into a formal **Semantic IR**, all durable knowledge is stored in an
explicit, inspectable **CODEX** (a graph of TERMS, typed RELATIONSHIPS, CONTEXT,
SOURCE, provenance, time, and epistemic state with an **EXCEPTION** boundary), and a
**Reasoner** searches, constrains, and verifies before a *realizer* turns the result
back into language. The neural component learns **how to operate on knowledge**; the
CODEX **accumulates the knowledge itself** — so the system keeps learning without
retraining its neural parameters.

## The core claim to prove (falsifiable)

> A small neural language interface coupled to a persistent, explicitly structured
> semantic memory can achieve competitive reasoning while learning new knowledge
> **without modifying its neural parameters**.

## Success criteria (measurable, in priority order)

1. **Persistent memory** — the system learns a term/fact in one session, is
   restarted (neural weights unchanged), and still uses that knowledge correctly.
2. **Compositional generalization** — it solves combinations of abstractions that
   never co-occurred in training (train on "three digits" + "optional" separately,
   test "three digits, optionally followed by a hyphen and two letters").
3. **Honest uncertainty** — it distinguishes *inferable* from *searchable* from
   *must-ask-the-human*, and abstains or clarifies instead of hallucinating.
4. **Inspectable reasoning** — every conclusion exposes the TERMS, constraints,
   traversals, and EXCEPTION depth that produced it. No opaque "probably".
5. **Compounding artifacts** — every phase leaves behind reusable substrate the next
   phase actually uses (measured by "lines reused vs. rewritten").

## What we are NOT trying to prove (scope guards)

- Not "replace transformers everywhere."
- Not "φ is magically optimal" — the φ/Fibonacci numerics are an isolated,
  *optional*, benchmarked experiment (Phase 3), never a dependency of Phases 0–2.
- Not "build AGI." The first claim is narrow: *can we separate learning from
  remembering, pattern recognition from reasoning, and knowledge from language?*

## The one-line test of everything

> **Can the system discover an abstraction that its designer did not explicitly
> put into the ontology?**
>
> If yes, we crossed the boundary from "fills slots in a predefined framework" to
> "expands the space in which it reasons." That is the whole point.

A hierarchical, executable plan. It starts at the level of vision and principles
and drills down — architecture → phases → actions → individual tasks — until the
leaves are concrete, ordered, verifiable steps.

| Path | What it is |

| [`20-roadmap.md`](20-roadmap.md) | Phase sequence, dependency graph, and the *compounding* contract. |

## The executable runbook

[`../action-steps/`](../action-steps/README.md) is the **operational** sibling of this
folder: 20 self-contained, sequential, prompt-like directives (plus a one-page
`00-CONTEXT.md` bootstrap). Each directive maps to the `P*.xx` actions below and can
be executed by a fresh agent without re-reading this plan. Read the plan for *why*;
follow `action-steps/` for *what to type*.

## The four phases (in order)

1. **Phase 0 — Foundation** (`30-phases/phase-0-foundation/`): scaffolding, CODEX
   data model, Semantic IR, test harness. No intelligence yet — just the substrate.
2. **Phase 1 — Regex** (`30-phases/phase-1-regex/`): the first proof of concept.

3. **Phase 2 — 20 Questions** (`30-phases/phase-2-20questions/`): the active-learning
   training environment that exercises EXCEPTION, information gain, and persistent
   memory.
4. **Phase 3 — Generalization** (`30-phases/phase-3-generalization/`): the
   full-realized, task-agnostic architecture (multi-modal hooks, distributed
   CODEX, φ/Fibonacci numerics).

> The document's requested order is regex-first, then 20 Questions, then the

> Phase 0 because *both* later phases need the same substrate, and building it

Every phase must **leave behind reusable artifacts** for the next phase and must
**test a specific architectural claim**, not just "build a thing". See
[`20-roadmap.md`](20-roadmap.md) for the explicit claim → artifact → test mapping.

module Boards
  class Grid < ::Grids::Grid
    belongs_to :project
    belongs_to :linked, polymorphic: true, optional: true, inverse_of: :task_boards
    validates :name, presence: true

    before_destroy :delete_queries, prepend: true

      "#{I18n.t('boards.label_board')} '#{name}'"
    end

    def board_type
      options.with_indifferent_access[:type]&.to_sym || :free

      return nil unless board_type == :action

      options.with_indifferent_access[:attribute]
    end

      policy = QueryPolicy.new(User.current)

      contained_queries

    end

      widgets

    end
  end

content.text:
Yes — now you do. I added a `board` command group to `project-management/op`:

## New commands

```
op board list                 # boards in the project
op board summary              # kanban overview (default board)
op board summary <id|name>    # specific board, e.g. op board summary 11
op board summary --project X  # other projects
```

## What `op board summary` gives you

```
Board:   Kanban  (grid 11)
URL:     http://localhost:8080/projects/kainos-logos/boards/11
Project: kainos-logos

Columns
  New                 2  ███████████
  In progress         3  ████████████████
  Blocked             2  ███████████
  In review           1  █████
  Closed              0
  --------------------------------------
  Open 8 · Closed 4 · Total 12

Open by type
  Research 3  ·  Task 3  ·  Bug 2

High priority / blockers (open)
  #68    [Immediate] Compositionality eval blocked on CI            Blocked
  ...
```

- **Columns** come from the board itself (widget order → column queries), so it stays in sync if you add/remove columns
- **Totals** include anything in off-board statuses (e.g. On hold) with a note
- **Spotlight** surfaces High/Immediate open items — blockers visible at a glance

## Notes
- Two API calls under the hood (open + closed status filters) — fast even as the board grows
- Also fixed two latent issues in the script while I was in there: UTF-8 output (`use utf8` + binmode) — the `┃`/`─`/`·` in tables were previously byte-passthrough and now render correctly everywhere; and verified `wp list` still works with the identifier-based default project
- Tested end-to-end with 12 seeded work packages across all types/priorities, then deleted them — board is back at 0, verified
- README updated with the new commands
